final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor provided no new admissible evidence and largely conceded the core audit points. Their response narrows the claim from broad certification to a disclosure-dependent, limited certification theory, but that is still not enough on the current record. The governing policy requires more than staged rollout, rollback, dashboards, or monitoring when the affected use case remains exposed: either exclusion of the affected use case or reviewed risk acceptance explaining why exposure is acceptable. The available summary states neither exists, and there is still no admissible evidence that the required disclosure is actually included in the certified packet at decision time. That makes this an unresolved compliance predicate, not merely a caveat. The Actor's reframing improves proportionality of description but does not cure the missing policy condition.
remaining_concerns: The student aid advising use case remains below target and exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
The rollout gate does not exclude the affected use case.
There is no approved risk acceptance addressing that exposure.
There is no admissible evidence that the required model-card disclosure is actually present in the certification packet or decision record.
The policy text says rollout controls and monitoring are insufficient when the affected segment remains exposed without exclusion or reviewed risk acceptance.
